Sol — Madrid, Spain

🟡 Local press research

Relatively safer day Average night

In detail

Sol (Puerta del Sol and adjoining Callao) has documented nighttime robbery incidents: in August 2025 Telemadrid and El Espanol reported a chain-snatching robbery and a violent attempted phone robbery within the same early-morning hour around Callao and Puerta del Sol, with three suspects arrested. General city-wide reporting also flags Centro as having high volumes of tourist-targeted pickpocketing. Night is rated yellow while day (heavy foot traffic, no comparable daytime incident reports found) remains green. Sources checked: Telemadrid, Aug 2025 (Noche de robos en Madrid: tres atracos en Callao y en Sol); El Espanol, Aug 2025; Telemadrid, Dec 2024 (metro pickpocketing, general).

Wandroz currently rates Sol in Madrid, Spain as relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Madrid, Spain during the day and roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Madrid, Spain at night. This comes from Wandroz's Level 2 approach: genuine, dated local/national press research for this specific area — not blind guessing, and not a fabricated statistic — but honestly disclosed as press-based rather than an official geolocated crime dataset, since none is publicly available for Madrid, Spain at this level of detail. Is Sol safe at night?

At night, Sol is rated as roughly average compared to other neighbourhoods in Madrid, Spain, based on the same press research. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Sol's day rating (relatively safer than most other neighbourhoods in Madrid, Spain) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late.
